label: Resolution Scale
help: Internal render scale. Pick by STABILITY, not just sharpness: 66% has been the most crash-stable, and 50% is oddly worse, not better. 85/90 are the headroom rungs: 90 renders ~19% fewer pixels than 100 (the GT HD slush-to-locked conversion test), 85 ~28% fewer (GT5P dyno ladder).

label: Audio Renderer Backend
help: Audio output path. Cubeb (via PipeWire) is the only real ROCKNIX choice; FAudio only exists if the build ships it; Null = silence for tests. (ALSA was never an RPCS3 backend -- old option here wrote an invalid config.)

label: Desired Buffer Duration
help: Audio latency buffer (ms; RPCS3 default 34). Absorbs scheduling JITTER only -- when the game produces audio slower than real-time (GT under full speed), no buffer size can save it; that is Time Stretching's job.

label: Enable Time Stretching
help: MASTER SWITCH -- the Threshold dial below is DEAD while this is OFF. Slows audio tempo (pitch-preserved, SoundTouch) when the buffer runs low, instead of leaving silent gaps. GT HD runs ON and sounds decent; GT5P has never had it ON.

label: Time Stretching Threshold
help: BUFFER-FILL %% below which stretching engages (needs the master switch ON; it is NOT an fps threshold). 100 = stretch whenever below target (GT HD's setting); lower = engage only under real starvation.

label: Disable Sampling Skip
help: When the game misses an audio period: OFF (default) waits up to ~21ms for late samples before skipping; ON advances immediately. Changes stutter texture (many small gaps vs fewer big ones) -- an A/B dial, not a cure.

label: PPU Threads
help: PS3 main-CPU worker threads. 2 is the SM8250 sweet spot; pushing higher steals the 8 cores the SPU/RSX threads need.

label: SPU Preferred Threads (0=Auto)
help: SPU worker pool size. OPERATOR-VALIDATED 2026-07-10: 3 keeps the MENUS springy while racing performance holds (auto/other values make menu navigation sluggish). The audio-only SPURS ladder (guest-side) is a different dial -- don't conflate.

label: Max SPURS Threads
help: Caps how many SPURS workers RUN concurrently per group (GT schedules audio/physics as SPURS jobs). 6 = stock. Lowering to 5/4 trades throughput for less core contention -- the Phase-3 audio-ladder dial; judge each rung by the ledger aud= skip/sil counts, not by ear alone.

label: SPU Block Size
help: SPU code-compilation granularity. OPERATOR-VALIDATED 2026-07-10: MEGA is REQUIRED for good GT5P performance on this rig -- Safe costs real framerate. Giga untested beyond spot checks; Mega is the certified setting.

label: SPU loop detection
help: Lets the SPU sleep in spin-loops to save power and heat. Safe to leave ON; rarely affects GT crashes.

label: Write Color Buffers
help: Writes rendered color back to memory -- fixes some GT6 visual glitches but costs fps. Once nudged the GPU-hang fault deeper (N=1).

label: Read Color Buffers
help: Reads the framebuffer back for effects (some GT mirror/replay views need it). OFF is faster; turn ON only if an effect is missing.

label: Write Depth Buffer
help: Writes the rendered depth buffer back to memory -- the depth-side analogue of Write Color Buffers. Costs fps; needed by a few depth-sampling effects. Note: does NOT fix the GT5P track-shadow flicker (that's upstream RPCS3 RSX bug #11912, no known setting cures it). OFF by default.

label: Read Depth Buffer
help: Reads the depth buffer back for effects that sample depth (shadows, soft particles). OFF is faster; turn ON if depth-based effects look stale or missing.

label: Strict Rendering Mode
help: Forces exact render-target handling instead of fast approximations -- can fix RTT/shadow glitches but a notable fps hit. A diagnostic/correctness lever; leave OFF unless chasing a visual bug.

label: Frame Limit
help: Caps fps. GT runs under 30 here anyway, so 'Off' lets it run free; a cap mainly steadies frametime and heat, not crashes.

label: Antialiasing
help: Edge smoothing. Disabled is the safe SM8250 pick -- buys fps; Auto looks cleaner but loads the GPU harder.

label: Multithreaded RSX
help: Splits PS3-GPU emulation onto its own thread. ON is faster on the 8-core SM8250; turn OFF only to isolate a bug.

label: Accurate RSX Reservation Access
help: Strict atomic ordering for RSX memory. More correct but slower; leave OFF unless you see corruption.

label: Shader Mode
help: Async multi-threaded is the only sane SM8250 choice; the others stall or are debug-only. WARNING: changing this invalidates the shader vault.

label: Min Scalable Dimension (px)
help: Smallest texture the upscaler touches. 16 upscales everything (sharper, heavier); higher skips small textures to save GPU.

label: Driver Wake-Up Delay
help: Pause (us) after submitting GPU work -- a coarse anti-fence-timeout knob. Higher can dodge some hangs at a frametime cost. Prefer the DRIVER-tab dials. Also shrinks recover_fifo's rapid-retry give-up window (RSXThread.cpp) -- pair with RSX FIFO Accuracy below.

label: RSX FIFO Accuracy
help: How strictly RPCS3 syncs its own emulated command-queue reads. Fast (current default) races the FIFO harder; Ordered & Atomic is what RPCS3's own error message recommends after a 'Dead FIFO commands queue' fatal (confirmed live 2026-07-01, ~35min into a session, distinct from the a6xx GPU-hang class -- RSXThread.cpp:2792 recover_fifo()). Trades CPU overhead for not racing the FIFO in the first place. Pair with Driver Wake-Up Delay.

label: Relaxed ZCULL Sync
help: Loosens depth-cull timing. ON boosts fps and GT tolerates it well; can cause minor pop-in.

label: Disable ZCull Occlusion Queries
help: Skips visibility queries entirely. Fps win, but can break HUD/visibility in some titles -- test per-game before trusting it.

label: Async Texture Streaming
help: Uploads textures off the render thread -- reduces hitching on big tracks. Small corruption risk; usually worth it for GT.

label: Force CPU Blit
help: Does image copies on the CPU instead of the GPU. A correctness fallback, usually slower -- leave OFF unless a game needs it.

label: Async Queue Scheduler
help: Vulkan submission scheduler. Fast lowers latency; Safe is steadier and is the SM8250 default.

label: Perf Overlay
help: RPCS3's OWN in-frame performance overlay (separate from the MangoHUD DDU -- both can show at once). This is the attribution instrument the DDU can't give: at Detail=High it splits the frame budget into PPU / SPU / RSX usage, so a pack-race bog finally says WHO ate the frame -- CPU emulation (PPU/SPU) or the GPU (RSX). Turn on with Detail=High for a pack stint, then off; it costs a little to draw.

label: Perf Overlay Detail
help: How much the Perf Overlay reports. HIGH is the one that matters: per-subsystem PPU%/SPU%/RSX% -- the pack-bog and audio-deficit attribution. Minimal/Low = fps + frametime only (redundant with the DDU). Only reads if Perf Overlay is on.

label: Perf Overlay Position
help: Which corner the Perf Overlay sits in. Park it OPPOSITE the DDU (DDU is bottom-left by default) so the two don't overlap -- Top Right is the safe pick.

label: Perf Frametime Graph
help: Draws the live frametime curve in the Perf Overlay -- the shape of the pacing, not just the number. Useful for SEEING a pack-section spike land vs a steady bog. Only reads if Perf Overlay is on.

label: Perf Overlay Interval (ms)
help: How often the Perf Overlay refreshes its numbers (RPCS3 default 350ms). Lower = twitchier read of a transient pack spike; higher = calmer average. Does not affect the frametime graph resolution.
